question: Find a non-constant shape with R > 2/3, and push it as high as possible.
stop: When the record has not improved by 0.0003 over the last 3 actions spanning at least 2 rounds.

question: Does exact-gradient optimization at higher discretization N (200 -> 1000+) improve R beyond the N=200 finite-difference result?
stop: When multi-resolution exact-gradient refinement has not raised the record by 0.0003 over 3 actions spanning at least 2 rounds.

question: Does concentrating f toward one edge (sparse support, f*f peak near the boundary) raise R beyond 0.833, and can extreme left-concentrated seeds find a better basin?
stop: When three actions on extreme-asymmetric seeds/refinement have not raised the record by 0.0003 over at least two rounds.

question: Does the new p0012 boundary-spike basin benefit from higher discretization N (400->800->1600) with exact-gradient reoptimization, unlike the p0011 basin?

Does higher discretization help only after structural tightening of the narrow spike, i.e. split each nonzero p0014 block into a half-width sub-block on an N=800/1600 grid, then exact-gradient reoptimize and perturb there?

Can corrected richer structural relocations (left-compress, spike move/split, block scale/zero) from p0014 push the extreme-boundary basin beyond 0.8735, and does repeated continuation keep yielding increments?
stop: When three actions of corrected structural relocation or continuation from p0014 have not raised the record by 0.0003 over at least two rounds.

outcome: Exhausted: richer structural relocation from p0014 gave p0018 only +0.000063, and a further 30 s continuation of p0014 (p0019) gave no change. The p0014/p0018 basin is effectively converged at N=400, so more tiny relocation is not the lever.

question: Can a fresh sparse multi-spike comb basin, optimized by exact-gradient L-BFGS-B, beat the extreme-edge single-spike basin (0.87357)?
stop: When three funded multi-spike fresh-basin actions have not raised the record by 0.0003 over at least two rounds.

question: Does a global coarse-to-fine multi-start over sparse spike shapes (optimized at N=64/100, then refined at N=400) find a basin better than the extreme-edge local optimum 0.87357?
Does exact zero-order-hold (step-preserving) upsampling to N=800/1600/3200 followed by exact-gradient refinement raise R beyond 0.87357, unlike linear-interpolation ladders?
stop: When two funded step-preserving refinement actions fail to raise the record by 0.0003.

outcome: Resolved negatively: exact ZOH upsampling to N=1600 and high-N perturb gave only +0.000013, so finer grids are not the missing lever.
Resolved negatively: a genuine coarse-to-fine global multi-start over thousands of seeds gave only +0.000010; coarse starts funnel into the same extreme-edge basin.
Resolved: exact zero-order-hold upsampling to N=800/1600 was tested (p0023) and gave only +0.000013, refuting the step-preserving-resolution hypothesis.

question: Can a non-local search (simulated annealing/basin-hopping that accepts worse states, or a continuous spike-position/width/height parameterization) escape the greedy L-BFGS plateau above 0.873584?
stop: When two funded non-local search actions fail to raise the record by 0.0003.
